attribution.note: Marcus wrote this in his own post, in his own voice.

semantics.note: Marcus says that on the post date Altman walked back his earlier hint that AGI was close. The proposition matches that.

contract.note: Reading 'walked it back' as publicly playing down near-term AGI, without needing a formal retraction, is how an ordinary reader would take it. It stretches nothing for or against Marcus.

evidence.note: A Decrypt report dated 2025-01-20 quotes Altman's X post: OpenAI has not built AGI, will not deploy it next month, and people should chill.
This is Decrypt's own reading of the post as a U-turn. It is commentary, not a separate record of the event.
A separate report from The Decoder, also dated 2025-01-20, confirms the same statement: AGI not built, cut expectations 100x.

reviews.rationale: Two independent same-day reports show that on 2025-01-20 Altman publicly played down near-term AGI: he said it had not been built, would not be deployed next month, and that expectations should be cut 100x. That meets the support condition. He never formally withdrew the 5 January sentence, but the contract does not require that.

attribution.note: Marcus wrote, in the third person, that he stands by his own prediction. He endorses it.

semantics.note: 'We will not see AGI in 2025' is a firm, unhedged forecast with a 2025 horizon. The Musk bet remark is rightly treated as context.

contract.note: Marcus gave no definition of AGI. The plain reading (no system widely accepted as AGI, and no verified formal declaration, in 2025) is ordinary and fair. Not counting loose remarks by insiders is reasonable.

evidence.note: The International AI Safety Report 2026, published Feb 2026 and covering systems up to Nov 2025, finds capabilities 'jagged', with failures on simpler tasks. That is not general human-level ability.

In the ARC Prize 2025 report, the organisers say AGI has not been achieved by their definition, and the top ARC-AGI-2 score was 24%. This is one benchmark, so it supports the outcome without deciding it.
Microsoft's 8-K exhibit from Oct 2025 describes AGI as not yet declared and sets up a panel to verify any declaration. It covers only up to late October.

A secondary forum timeline recording Altman's loose Dec 2025 'whooshing by' remark. That is an informal insider remark, not a verified declaration. The item's available_at (Feb 2026) does not match the comment's 10 Mar 2026 date.

reviews.rationale: The horizon ended on 2025-12-31. Independent assessments of late 2025 describe uneven capabilities, the main general-reasoning benchmark was far from solved, and no formal AGI declaration had been made as of Oct 2025. Altman's informal December remark is not wide acceptance or a verified declaration, so it does not meet the contradiction condition. The forecast held under the contract's plain reading.
